title: Gottfried van Swieten (Bonn) to Count Cobenzl, undated (1757-58) (ARA Brussels SEG 1236 f. 141; DECODE R955)

documents.shelfmark: ARA Brussels, Secretairerie d'Etat et de Guerre inv. 1236 f. 141; DECODE R955

plaintext.source: The clear text written below the numbers is the decipherment.

transcription.notes: DECODE digits checked against the images; runs with dropped or doubled digits re-read from the scans.

system.summary: Three-digit alphabetical syllabary of 1757 (202-586): letters at the head of their sections, then their syllables, with a few homophones.
system.sibling_key: The 1759 table of swieten1759 (R956, R957): same design, different numbers.
system.notes: R955 groups are dot-separated. The 1759 letters (R956, R957) are a separate entry, swieten1759.

prior_solution.where: The decipherment is written below the numbers on f. 141 itself.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE R955-R957 fetched with the session cookie (8 page images, 3 transcriptions); R955 is this entry.
Web search and local Tomokiyo/cryptiana copies for a printed decipherment.
R955: the clear lines under the numbers are the decipherment; aligned, they give an alphabetical syllabary (a 203, de 282, on 435, re 472...).

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R955 (1757 table, 202-586, read from the decipherment on its own page) stays in swieten1757; R956/R957 (the 1759 table, 100-442, rebuilt ciphertext-only) moved to swieten1759 with msolve.py, dec.py, key.json, overrides.json, runs.txt, validation.tsv. A reveal of R955 was built from the 1757 values in NOTES.md (build_reveal955.py): 86 of 89 groups valued.

outcome.method_basis: The clear lines written under the numbers on f. 141 are the decipherment of the ciphered sentence; aligned with the groups they give the 1757 alphabetical syllabary.

gaps.detail: each occurs once; the decipherment gives the word but not the split

outcome.notes: Read at the time; the 1757 table recovered from the alignment.

credits.note: decipherment written below the numbers of R955 (f. 141)

outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher/R955.txt (89 groups): every group falls under the contemporary decipherment; 86 of them carry a value in the aligned 1757 table (NOTES.md), 400, 297 and 586 inside "conclure même" do not.
